title: SSC CGL Tier-2 — Mock Test 6
description: Full-length 100-question mock simulating the latest SSC CGL Tier-1 pattern. 60 minutes total, no sectional timing, 2 marks/Q, -0.5 negative. Includes 5 inline Current-Affairs questions in the GA section (Fiscal deficit FY25-26, AI Impact Summit, CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Bhubaneswar 2028, BioAsia 2026) — refreshable from the admin CA pool.

questions.stem: Find the missing term: 3, 8, 18, 38, 78, ?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.explanation: Differences: A→C(+2), C→F(+3), F→J(+4), J→O(+5), O→U(+6). Next = U.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, 'PEN' is written as 'NCL'. How is 'INK' written?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts −2: P→N, E→C, N→L. Apply to INK: I→G, N→L, K→I → GLI.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 'TEACHER' is coded as '20-5-1-3-8-5-18', how is 'CHILD' coded?
questions.explanation: Letter→position: A=1...Z=26. C=3, H=8, I=9, L=12, D=4.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 'EARTH' is coded as 'GCTVJ', how is 'MOON' coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +2: E→G, A→C, R→T, T→V, H→J. Apply to MOON: M→O, O→Q, O→Q, N→P → OQQP.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, '#@$%' represents 'GOOD' (with letter pattern). If 'GOOD' = '@##$', then 'WOOD' is encoded by changing 'G' to 'W'. The number of distinct symbols used to spell GOOD is:
questions.explanation: GOOD has 4 letters but only 3 distinct ones: G, O, D (O appears twice). So 3 distinct symbols suffice.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, 'STUDY' is written as 'TUVEZ'. How is 'EXAM' written?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +1: S→T, T→U, U→V, D→E, Y→Z. Apply to EXAM: E→F, X→Y, A→B, M→N → FYBN.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A is the husband of B, and C is the only daughter of A and B, how is C related to A's only son D?
questions.explanation: A and B have a daughter C and a son D. So C and D are siblings. C is D's sister.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Pointing to a photograph, Mohan said, 'He is the son of my father's only son.' How is the boy in the photograph related to Mohan?
questions.explanation: Mohan's father's only son = Mohan himself (assuming he has no brother). So 'son of myself' = Mohan's son.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If P is the brother of Q, Q is the sister of R, and R is the daughter of S, how is P related to S?
questions.explanation: R is S's daughter; Q is R's sister, so Q is also S's daughter; P is Q's brother, so P is S's son.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Sita walks 6 km west, then turns north and walks 8 km. How far is she from her starting point?
questions.explanation: 6-8-10 right triangle: distance = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Sunita walks 5 km North, turns east and walks 12 km. How far is she from the start?
questions.explanation: 5-12-13 right triangle: distance = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All doctors are human. All humans need rest.

Conclusions:
I. All doctors need rest.
II. Some humans are doctors.
questions.explanation: I: Doctors ⊂ Humans, Humans need rest ⟹ Doctors need rest. TRUE. II: All doctors are human ⟹ some humans are doctors. TRUE. Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: No politician is honest. Some leaders are politicians.

Conclusions:
I. Some leaders are not honest.
II. All leaders are politicians.
questions.explanation: I: Some leaders are politicians; no politicians are honest ⟹ some leaders are not honest. TRUE. II: 'Some leaders are politicians' does NOT mean 'all leaders are politicians'. FALSE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A > B, B = C, and C ≥ D, which of the following is DEFINITELY TRUE?
questions.explanation: A > B = C ≥ D ⟹ A > D. TRUE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statement: India has imposed a ban on single-use plastic items.

Course of Action:
I. Citizens should be educated about alternatives.
II. Heavy fines should be imposed on violators.
questions.explanation: Both education AND enforcement (fines) are necessary for a ban to succeed. Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Choose the odd one out:
questions.explanation: Mango, Apple, Orange are fruits. Carrot is a vegetable.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five people P, Q, R, S, T sit in a row. P is at the extreme left. R is to the immediate right of Q. S is between R and T. Q is to the immediate right of P. Who is at the extreme right?
questions.explanation: P at left. Q right of P (P-Q). R right of Q (P-Q-R). S between R and T (P-Q-R-S-T). T at extreme right.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 1 January 2025 is a Wednesday, what day is 1 January 2026?
questions.explanation: 2025 is NOT a leap year (365 days). 365 mod 7 = 1 odd day. Wednesday + 1 = Thursday.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A cube of side 4 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have only ONE face painted?
questions.explanation: Cubes with exactly 1 face painted lie at the centre of each face. Per face: (n−2)² = 2² = 4. Total faces = 6, so 6 × 4 = 24.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Find the missing number:

3 | 5 | 7
9 | 25 | 49
27 | 125 | ?
questions.explanation: Per column: top=base, middle=base², bottom=base³. Col 1: 3, 9, 27 ✓. Col 2: 5, 25, 125 ✓. Col 3: 7, 49, ? ⟹ 7³ = 343.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: DAY : NIGHT :: GROW : ?
questions.explanation: Day and Night are antonyms. Antonym of Grow is Shrink.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the establishment of an inter-state council?
questions.explanation: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council to coordinate between states.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who has the authority to dissolve the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The President dissolves the Lok Sabha on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister (Article 85).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
questions.explanation: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Concept of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from:
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) are borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which is the Supreme Court's largest Bench by number of judges in a particular case?
questions.explanation: A Constitutional Bench (5 or more judges) hears constitutional matters. It is the largest bench size.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The 'Khilafat Movement' was launched by Indian Muslims in support of:
questions.explanation: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was launched in support of the Ottoman Caliphate after WWI. Gandhi linked it with the Non-Cooperation Movement.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who established the Indian National Army (INA)?
questions.explanation: The INA was established in 1942 by Captain Mohan Singh. Subhas Chandra Bose later assumed leadership in 1943.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire in 321 BCE, with the political guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which Indian state is the largest producer of tea?
questions.explanation: Assam is India's largest tea producer, accounting for over 50% of national production.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The 'Black Soil' is most extensively found in which Indian region?
questions.explanation: Black soil (Regur) is found extensively in the Deccan Plateau, especially in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and parts of Andhra Pradesh.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The 'Nine Degree Channel' separates:
questions.explanation: The Nine Degree Channel separates the Lakshadweep islands from the Minicoy island.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The metal used in making thermometers is:
questions.explanation: Mercury is used in thermometers because it's a liquid metal at room temperature with high coefficient of thermal expansion.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which organ in the human body produces insulin?
questions.explanation: Insulin is produced by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The unit of pressure is:
questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in Pascals (Pa). 1 Pa = 1 N/m².
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which of the following is responsible for converting nitrogen in the atmosphere to nitrogen compounds in plants?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria (e.g., Rhizobium in root nodules of legumes) convert atmospheric nitrogen (N₂) into compounds usable by plants.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: 'Project Tiger' was launched in India in which year?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched in April 1973 to protect the Bengal Tiger and its habitat in India.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which Mughal emperor is known as 'Zinda Pir'?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb is called 'Zinda Pir' (Living Saint) for his religious orthodoxy and austere lifestyle.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form from Kerala, characterized by graceful, swaying movements.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who wrote the famous epic 'Ramcharitmanas'?
questions.explanation: Ramcharitmanas was composed by Goswami Tulsidas in the 16th century in Awadhi (a dialect of Hindi).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which is the highest mountain peak in India?
questions.explanation: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) is the highest peak located entirely within India (in Sikkim). K2 is in Pakistan-administered Kashmir; Everest is on the Nepal-China border.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: As per the 2026 Union Budget, India's fiscal deficit target for FY 2025-26 is approximately:
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2026 set the fiscal deficit target at 4.4% of GDP for FY 2025-26, continuing the path of fiscal consolidation.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which institute hosted India's flagship 'AI Impact Summit' in 2026?
questions.explanation: The AI Impact Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi in February 2026.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: In February 2026, who took oath as the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India?
questions.explanation: Gyanesh Kumar took oath as the 26th CEC of India in February 2026.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Bhubaneswar will host which championship in 2028?
questions.explanation: Bhubaneswar (Odisha) was awarded the hosting rights for the 2028 Asian Athletics Championships.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: BioAsia 2026, India's flagship life-sciences conference, was held in which city?
questions.explanation: BioAsia 2026 was hosted in Hyderabad — the flagship life-sciences conference of Telangana.

questions.stem: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours, another in 15 hours. If both pipes are opened together, in how many hours will the tank fill?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/15 = (5+4)/60 = 9/60 = 3/20 per hour. Time = 20/3 hours = 6 hr 40 min.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a platform 250 m long in 25 seconds. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanation: Speed = 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Distance = 20 × 25 = 500 m. Length of train = 500 − 250 = 250 m.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: A man rows downstream 18 km in 2 hours and upstream 8 km in 2 hours. Find his speed in still water.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 18/2 = 9 km/h. Upstream speed = 8/2 = 4 km/h. Speed in still water = (9+4)/2 = 6.5 km/h.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: Two cars start at the same time from cities 240 km apart. They move towards each other at speeds 50 km/h and 70 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 50 + 70 = 120 km/h. Time = 240/120 = 2 hours.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: If x + y = 10 and xy = 21, find x² + y².
questions.explanation: (x+y)² = x² + 2xy + y² ⟹ 100 = x² + y² + 42 ⟹ x² + y² = 58.

questions.stem: Choose the most appropriate word for blank (1).
questions.passage_context: Indian sports have witnessed __(1)__ growth over the past two decades. From a country known mainly for cricket, India has now produced world-class athletes in disciplines as varied as badminton, wrestling, and chess. Government schemes such as Khelo India and TOPS have __(2)__ played a role in identifying and supporting young talent. However, infrastructure outside the metro cities still remains __(3)__ in many rural pockets. Coaches, scientific training facilities, and access to international competition are all areas where __(4)__ investment is required. questions.stem: Which of the following best captures the author's overall view?
questions.passage_context: The Digital India initiative, launched in 2015, has transformed the way citizens interact with government services. Aadhaar, the biometric ID system, now covers over 1.3 billion residents, enabling Direct Benefit Transfers that have plugged leaks worth an estimated ₹2.7 lakh crore. UPI has emerged as the world's leading instant-payments platform, processing over 13 billion transactions monthly by 2025. Yet challenges persist. Data privacy frameworks, while now in place via the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, require robust enforcement. Cybersecurity incidents have grown alongside digitisation. Inclusive access also remains a concern — rural broadband penetration, while improving rapidly, has not yet matched urban levels. The next phase of Digital India must balance ambitious adoption with rigorous safeguards and equitable reach.
options: Digital India has been a complete success
Digital India has had major successes but faces real challenges
questions.explanation: The passage celebrates achievements while highlighting privacy, security, and access challenges.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the FIRST sentence.

(A) Yet adoption rates remain uneven across age groups.
(B) The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated India's shift to digital payments.
(C) Younger users embrace UPI quickly; older users still prefer cash.
(D) Government and banks have launched targeted campaigns to bridge this gap.
(E) The success of these efforts will determine the pace of full digital inclusion.
questions.explanation: B (intro: pandemic accelerated digital) → A (yet uneven) → C (specifics) → D (response) → E (closing). 1st = B.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the FOURTH sentence.

(A) The Indian space programme began modestly in the 1960s.
(B) Initial focus was on satellite-based communication and weather forecasting.
(C) Over the decades, ISRO mastered launch vehicle technology.
(D) The Mars Orbiter Mission of 2014 was a landmark achievement.
(E) Today, India is a recognised global player in space exploration.
questions.explanation: A (intro) → B (early focus) → C (decades of growth) → D (landmark mission) → E (current status). 4th = D.
questions.subject: ENGLISH
